svg.aria-label: The chemical nature of DNA methylation and the two mechanisms that lower transcription: methylation at carbon five of cytosine and the symmetry of the CpG arrangement, the difference in target molecule from histone methylation, the position and property of CpG islands, direct obstruction of transcription factor binding, and the route by which a methyl-CpG binding protein brings in a repressive complex.
svg.text: A Same word, different target molecule
histone methylation to a PROTEIN residue (Lys, Arg)
DNA methylation to the BASE cytosine, carbon 5
B CpG and its symmetry
CpG means C followed by G ON THE SAME STRAND. The p is the
phosphate — do not read it as the C-G base pair.
The opposite strand is also CpG, so BOTH strands can carry the mark.
That symmetry is the basis of the maintenance mechanism in section 8.
Methylation is not a mutation: the base is not exchanged, a group is added.
Ordinary sequencing misses it; bisulfite treatment is needed.
C CpG island
CpG island
gene
Present at the promoter of about 60 percent of human genes.
CpG is rare genome-wide because 5mC deaminates to T and CpG
was lost over time; islands escaped that loss, which implies they
stayed unmethylated in most cells.
D Two mechanisms that lower transcription
1 DIRECT: some factors cannot bind their recognition sequence when a methyl group sits on it — the group masks the binding surface.
2 READER: MeCP2 and MBD proteins recognise methylated CpG and bring in corepressors with HDAC. This acts over a wider range, since the chromatin change can spread.
TF
MeCP2
HDAC cx
Caveat: gene-body methylation is HIGH in actively transcribed genes, and at an imprinting control region methylation changes an enhancer's reach instead. Always check WHICH region was measured.
